classification.difficultyReason: Combine separate percentage changes to weekly earnings and working hours before calculating an hourly rate.

content.prompt: Fred Callum earns a salary of $\$450$ per week for a 40-hour week. His weekly salary is increased by $10\%$ and his number of hours worked is decreased by $10\%$. Calculate his new hourly salary.

answer.short:
$\$13.75$ per hour.

Divide the increased weekly salary by the reduced weekly hours.
answer.worked: $$\begin{align*}\text{Weekly salary increase}&=\frac{10}{100}\times\$450\\\text{Weekly salary increase}&=\$45\\\text{New weekly salary}&=\$450+\$45\\\text{New weekly salary}&=\$495\\\text{Reduction in weekly hours}&=\frac{10}{100}\times40\\\text{Reduction in weekly hours}&=4\\\text{New weekly hours}&=40-4\\\text{New weekly hours}&=36\\\text{New hourly salary}&=\frac{\$495}{36}\\\text{New hourly salary}&=\$13.75\text{ per hour}\end{align*}$$
